---
title: "F-test heterogeneity designs"
description: "Generate temporal and cohort alternatives for joint tests of treatment-effect homogeneity."
jupyter: python3
---

These designs support the public
[TestingInEventStudies](https://github.com/apoorvalal/TestingInEventStudies)
project and the paper [When can we get away with using the two-way fixed effects
regression?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.05125). The package generates the null
and alternative effect surfaces. It does not implement the test statistic.

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from pypanelsim import designs
```

## Two different heterogeneity questions

The temporal family asks whether the effect is constant over exposure time. It
uses one treatment cohort.

The cohort family asks whether adoption cohorts share the same event-time path.
It uses three cohorts and correlated untreated errors.

```{python}
print("temporal:", designs.available_ftest_temporal_designs())
print("cohort:", designs.available_ftest_cohort_designs())
```

## Temporal alternatives

The seven paths are constant, linear, concave, positive-then-negative,
exponential, sinusoidal, and random walk.

```{python}
temporal_config = designs.FTestTemporalConfig(
    n_units=240,
    n_periods=35,
    adoption_period=15,
    max_effect=1.0,
)

for name in designs.available_ftest_temporal_designs():
    profile = designs.ftest_temporal_profile(
        name,
        config=temporal_config,
        seed=42,
    )
    print(name, np.round(profile[:6], 2))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-ftest-temporal-profiles
#| fig-cap: "The seven single-cohort temporal effect alternatives."
#| fig-alt: "Seven small line charts show constant, linear, plateau, hump, delayed, sign-changing, and fading temporal effect paths."

temporal_names = designs.available_ftest_temporal_designs()
figure, axes = plt.subplots(
    2,
    4,
    figsize=(13, 7),
    sharex=True,
    constrained_layout=True,
)
for axis, name in zip(axes.ravel(), temporal_names, strict=False):
    profile = designs.ftest_temporal_profile(
        name,
        config=temporal_config,
        seed=42,
    )
    axis.plot(np.arange(profile.size), profile, marker="o", markersize=3)
    axis.axhline(0.0, color="black", linewidth=0.6)
    axis.set_title(name.replace("_", " "))
    axis.set_xlabel("event time")
    axis.set_ylabel("effect")
for axis in axes.ravel()[len(temporal_names):]:
    axis.set_visible(False)
plt.show()
```

The untreated outcome contains unit effects, time effects, small unit trends,
and AR(1) error. The treatment path begins at `adoption_period`.

```{python}
temporal_panel = designs.ftest_temporal(
    "positive_then_negative",
    config=temporal_config,
    profile_seed=42,
    seed=17,
)

print(temporal_panel.shape)
print(round(temporal_panel.true_att, 3))
```

`profile_seed` fixes the random-walk alternative itself. `seed` controls the
panel draw. Keeping these inputs separate prevents a change in outcome noise
from changing the effect profile.

## Cohort alternatives

The cohort family uses three adoption dates. Named surfaces range from a
homogeneous null to large cohort differences and selection on gains.

```{python}
cohort_config = designs.FTestCohortConfig(n_units=240)

for name in designs.available_ftest_cohort_designs():
    profiles = designs.ftest_cohort_profiles(name, config=cohort_config)
    first_values = {
        cohort: round(float(path[0]), 2)
        for cohort, path in profiles.items()
    }
    print(name, first_values)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-ftest-cohort-profiles
#| fig-cap: "Cohort-specific paths for the seven effect-surface alternatives."
#| fig-alt: "Seven small line charts compare cohort-specific effect paths under the F-test heterogeneity alternatives."

cohort_names = designs.available_ftest_cohort_designs()
figure, axes = plt.subplots(
    2,
    4,
    figsize=(14, 7),
    sharex=True,
    constrained_layout=True,
)
for axis, name in zip(axes.ravel(), cohort_names, strict=False):
    profiles = designs.ftest_cohort_profiles(name, config=cohort_config)
    for cohort, profile in profiles.items():
        axis.plot(
            np.arange(profile.size),
            profile,
            label=f"cohort {cohort}",
        )
    axis.axhline(0.0, color="black", linewidth=0.6)
    axis.set_title(name.replace("_", " "))
    axis.set_xlabel("event time")
    axis.set_ylabel("effect")
for axis in axes.ravel()[len(cohort_names):]:
    axis.set_visible(False)
axes.ravel()[0].legend(fontsize=7)
plt.show()
```

Run one surface and inspect its supported cohort-event truth:

```{python}
cohort_panel = designs.ftest_cohort(
    "selection_on_gains",
    config=cohort_config,
    seed=17,
)

truth = cohort_panel.truth.cohort_event(event_times=(-2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3))
for cohort in np.unique(truth["cohort"]):
    selected = truth["cohort"] == cohort
    print(
        int(cohort),
        np.round(truth["effect"][selected], 2),
        truth["supported"][selected],
    )
```

Pre-treatment effects are zero. An unsupported cohort-event cell has `NaN`
effect and `supported=False`.

## Realized panel structure

The temporal design has one adoption block. The cohort design has three. The
outcome heatmaps also show their different untreated dependence structures.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ftest-realized-panels
#| fig-cap: "Observed outcomes and treatment for one temporal and one cohort-heterogeneity design."
#| fig-alt: "Four heatmaps show observed outcomes and treatment for one temporal-effect alternative and one cohort-heterogeneity alternative."

realized_panels = (
    ("Temporal alternative", temporal_panel),
    ("Cohort alternative", cohort_panel),
)
figure, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(13, 8), constrained_layout=True)
for row, (label, draw) in enumerate(realized_panels):
    order = np.argsort(draw.adoption_times, kind="stable")
    outcome_image = axes[row, 0].matshow(
        draw.outcome[order],
        aspect="auto",
        cmap="coolwarm",
    )
    axes[row, 1].matshow(
        draw.treatment[order],
        aspect="auto",
        cmap="Greys",
        vmin=0.0,
        vmax=1.0,
    )
    axes[row, 0].set_title(f"{label}: outcome")
    axes[row, 1].set_title(f"{label}: treatment")
    axes[row, 0].set_ylabel("units, sorted by adoption")
    figure.colorbar(outcome_image, ax=axes[row, 0], fraction=0.03, pad=0.02)
    for axis in axes[row]:
        axis.set_xlabel("period")
plt.show()
```

## Build a custom cohort surface

The configured family uses the same primitives that are available to user
code. A cohort surface is a map from adoption period to an event-time array.

```{python}
from pypanelsim import primitives

profiles = designs.ftest_cohort_profiles(
    "novelty_effects",
    config=cohort_config,
)
effect_model = primitives.CohortEventTimeEffect(profiles)

print(type(effect_model).__name__)
```

Pass this effect model to a custom `core.PanelSimulator` when the built-in
untreated outcome or assignment law is not appropriate.

## Simulation-study use

A size experiment should use a homogeneous design as its null. A power
experiment should vary the form and magnitude of heterogeneity. Report the
exact named surface, configuration, panel seed, and any profile seed. Do not
refer only to “the F-test DGP”; that phrase does not identify one probability
law.
